articles.title_orig: Nvidia CEO’s affair with an alleged Chinese spy could be a problem for the economy
articles.title_zh: Nvidia CEO’s affair with an alleged Chinese spy could be a problem for the economy
articles.content_orig:
Rep. John Moolenaar , R-Mich., said on a Tuesday appearance on CNBC's "Squawk Box" that Congress needs to "get to the bottom" of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang 's affair with an alleged Chinese spy.
Moolenaar, who chairs the House Permanent Select Committee on China, said he wants to know whether Huang shared privileged information with a Chinese spy; whether Huang was influenced to lobby against preventing chip sales to China; and whether China was given preference in purchasing Nvidia's limited supply of advanced chips.
And he urged a thorough internal investigation of Huang.
"If it becomes less of an investigation, more of damage control, that's not going to work because people have to have confidence," Moolenaar said.
"We're dealing with the country, the Chinese Communist Party that is a foremost adversary, that's funding wars and supporting Russia, supporting Iran, North Korea," he said. "And we have basically a Cold War race with technology. We cannot allow the premier company at the forefront of this to, in some way, be irresponsible."
Congressional scrutiny of Huang's affair has intensified since members returned to Washington on Monday.
The New York Times reported that Huang was romantically involved with Alice Huang, a Megaspeed executive who U.S. intelligence agencies have identified as a Chinese intelligence asset. Nvidia opened an investigation into its CEO on Sunday. The two Huangs are not related.
House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries , D-N.Y., said in a press conference on Monday that "we're going to need a full briefing specifically as it relates to the Nvidia issue so we can all get to the bottom of what has happened and what the implications are in terms of national security"
Moolenaar co-authored a letter with Florida Rep. Brian Mast and Arkansas Rep. Rick Crawford on Nov. 5 asking Huang to appear before the Select Committee on China, the House Foreign Affairs Committee and House Select Committee on Intelligence. Mast chairs the foreign affairs panel, and Crawford chairs intelligence.
"Recent reports raise significant national security concerns regarding the PRC's access to sensitive U.S. technology and information," the three Republicans wrote.

articles.title_orig: Moonshot AI rented restricted Nvidia AI chips inside China, documents show
articles.title_zh: Moonshot AI rented restricted Nvidia AI chips inside China, documents show
articles.content_orig:
By ANDREW JEHRING, CHIEF FOREIGN CORRESPONDENT and JOHN-PAUL FORD ROJAS, DEPUTY BUSINESS EDITOR
Published: 19:17 EST, 9 November 2026 | Updated: 22:08 EST, 9 November 2026
The Chinese 'spy' accused of honey-trapping the boss of the world's biggest AI chip firm had bragged that she could secure his firm's technology despite a US export ban.
Alice Huang pitched a deal to Beijing investors to secure Nvidia's coveted graphics processing units (GPUs) last year.
Ms Huang said she had 'no problem securing GPUs', the Financial Times reported, even though Chinese firms are barred from obtaining them by the US.
She did not disclose her relationship with Nvidia's married chief executive Jensen Huang, who is no relation, during the investment pitch for a data centre project in Singapore .
Washington imposed strict limits on the US firm's exports to thwart attempts by Chinese president Xi Jinping to become the leading AI superpower by 2030.
Nvidia went into meltdown on Monday after Mr Huang admitted having an affair with Ms Huang months after she was declared a Chinese spy by US intelligence.
On Sunday, the 63-year-old said in a memo to staff: 'I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did.'
The company has commissioned an independent probe into the affair. It lost around £292billion of its value – or 9 per cent – in minutes on Monday, equal to the combined value of HSBC and Barclays. Its shares recovered, but it was still down by 4 per cent by the evening, making it worth around £3trillion.
Nvidia Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang is pictured at a party with suspected Chinese spy Alice Huang in June 2024
Mr Huang admitted he was 'unfaithful' to his wife, Lori Huang, who he is pictured with her during a visit to the White House on September 24
Ms Huang apparently worked as a Chinese state TV reporter and had a stint in private equity before she formed Megaspeed International in 2023, according to unverified internet biographies.
Within a year the previously dormant firm became the largest buyer of Nvidia's chips in south-east Asia. Weeks before they started purchasing the chips she was seen drinking whisky with Taiwan-born American businessman Mr Huang in Taipei – the first known pictures of them together.
Megaspeed's imports topped £3.6billion as it opened facilities across south-east Asia and rented the firm's technology to the Chinese tech giant Alibaba.
The investments set off alarm bells in Washington and Ms Huang was placed under surveillance at the end of 2024. Earlier this year she was named as a spy in a US intelligence report.
However, Donald Trump – a close ally of Mr Huang – did nothing, the New York Times reported.
Theresa Fallon, director of the Centre for Russia Europe Asia Studies in Brussels, said: 'It is always amazing to see how so-called intelligent people fall for a Chinese honey-trap.'
Rush Doshi, an assistant security studies professor at Georgetown University in Washington, said: 'If the reporting is right, this is the most significant story in US-China policy in years.
'If the US knew Jensen Huang had a romantic relationship with a Chinese spy and looked the other way, all while that spy ran a company backdooring US compute to China, it warrants a Congressional investigation.'
America restricted firms from exporting advanced Nvidia chips to China in 2022, but some smuggled them illegally over the border. Others legally set up businesses that buy large numbers of chips to build data centres in south-east Asia that serve Chinese firms.
Ms Huang apparently worked as a Chinese state TV reporter and had a stint in private equity before she formed Megaspeed International in 2023, according to unverified internet biographies
Mr Huang is pictured with President Donald Trump last month
Megaspeed, based in Singapore, appeared to be a middle man, buying Nvidia chips and providing computing power to Chinese firms operating outside the country. However, it was suspected of smuggling the tech into China.
Mr Huang lobbied Mr Trump to relax export laws on chips, and when a US delegation visited China last May he was initially left off the list due to concerns about his 'influence on the President's policy of only lightly regulating AI'.
Silicon Valley giants defended the tech tycoon last night. Shaun Maguire, a partner at Sequoia Capital, a tech investment firm, tweeted that Mr Huang was 'irreplaceable for America's AI leadership', adding: 'My guess is there was no bad intention.' SpaceX boss Elon Musk said: 'I agree.'
Wall Street hedge fund manager Bill Ackman said: 'Jensen Huang is human. And he is an incredible human... even incredible humans make mistakes.'
China denied Ms Huang was a spy and accused the US of 'groundless smears and slanders'.
Nvidia said it 'prioritises US national and economic security' but 'has no reason to believe that either national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised.
It added that Mr Huang was co-operating with its investigation and would remain as chief executive pending the review.

By FREDA LEWIS-STEMPEL, SENIOR MOTORING REPORTER
Updated: 04:29 EST, 10 November 2026
The Government is expected to slash EV sales targets this week after intense lobbying by carmakers and the motor industry.
The move would see the current targets for new car sales in the UK – which require four in five new cars sold to be fully electric by 2030 – cut significantly, sources say.
Currently, the Zero Emission Vehicle (ZEV) mandate scheme requires manufacturers to sell an increasing proportion of fully electric cars each year, rising from 33 per cent this year to the 80 per cent figure by 2030.
By 2035, all new car sales will need to be electric, but the speed at which the phase-out happens has been debated, with manufacturers demanding lower targets and the Government subsequently launching a review of the ZEV mandate in August .
With the consultation now closed, the Government is expected to announce a significant reduction to the percentage of new cars that need to be all-electric by 2030, allowing more hybrid vehicles to be sold by that date instead.
If the proposed cut comes in, carmakers will be given more flexibility and drivers will be able to buy new combustion-engined cars for longer in Britain.
The Government is expected to announce this week that it will reduce its EV sales targets, giving manufacturers more flexibility and allowing for more hybrid models to be sold
Cabinet Minister Louise Haigh – previously Secretary of State for Transport from 2024 to 2024 – is expected to make an announcement this week after a crunch meeting on Wednesday, yet Downing Street insists no decision has been made.
According to Press Association, Burnham was asked on Monday during a visit to Watford about the watering down of EV targets.
He said: 'Well, the consultation on the mandate for zero-emission vehicles concluded only a fortnight ago, so obviously that is being looked at now...The range of responses to the consultation… so these reports are just that: they’re reports, they’re speculation and no decision has been made at this point.'
However, speculation continues to circulate following the EU's backing of proposals last week to allow more combustion-engined cars to be sold after 2035 as it looks to dilute its own ban on new petrol and diesel vehicles.
Industry experts warn that continually moving goalposts on when combustion engine cars will be removed from showrooms for good creates uncertainty for manufacturers and hurts consumer confidence.
Rob Hull, the Daily Mail's motoring editor, earlier this year said: 'Trying to tell you how much longer you'll be able to buy a new petrol car has become guesswork.
'And the consequence of all this indecision is far more serious for Britain's motor industry. Carmakers are already grappling with soaring energy costs, increased export tariffs and relentless competition from China.
'Constantly shifting the deadline only makes it harder for them to plan, invest and compete.
'After nearly a decade of arbitrary deadlines and political U-turns like this latest one, Britain doesn't need another consultation or another delay. It needs certainty. Pick a date. Commit to it. And, for once, stick to it.'
Is the government right to ease EV targets, or is it putting climate goals in jeopardy to protect carmakers?
The change would be the second time Labour has downgraded its 2030 hard ban on sales of new combustion engine cars; in 2025, it relaxed the rules to allow hybrids to stay in showrooms until 2035 to appease those not wanting to switch to an EV.
A government spokesman said: 'The Government is united in its commitment to the ZEV Mandate, and no decisions have been taken.
'We are committed to the phase out of all new cars relying solely on petrol and diesel engines by 2030, and to 100 per cent of new car and van sales being zero emission by 2035, and our legally binding net zero targets.
'Our consultation on the Mandate will not change this, and will ensure we are taking a pragmatic and balanced approach to the ZEV transition.'
If the Government allows for more hybrids to be sold then drivers not ready to commit to an EV will be able to choose from better, more affordable hybrid models
If the Government does water down the ZEV threshold from 80 per cent to 55 per cent, allowing carmakers to sell more hybrids and plug-in hybrids, the range of new models available to buyers will increase.
Drivers not ready to commit to an EV will be able to choose from better, more affordable hybrid models across more vehicle body types.
Chinese newcomers such as Chery are offering efficient and affordable 'super hybrids' across their brands, enticing buyers with EV-only ranges of up to 93 miles and total combined ranges of 745 miles, while European legacy brands are competing by offering PHEVs with 88 miles of range – such as the Audi A3 TFSI e.
With the EU also relaxing its EV-only sales deadline, legacy brands are likely to continue production of cars with hybrid engines for longer and in greater volumes.
And given the scale of manufacturing in China, many of the newcomer brands to Britain have the capacity to adjust to a shifting target, meaning a range of fresh hybrid vehicles could emerge over the next decade.
2. EVs could become more expensive
If the ZEV mandate is relaxed and manufacturers face less pressure to discount EVs before 2030, upfront EV prices could rise.
On average, manufacturers have been discounting by around £11,000 per vehicle, according to SMMT analysis.
However, carmakers are working round the clock to bring down new EV prices – the cheapest model in the UK costs just £11,990 – so technological and manufacturing advances may offset this problem.
3. Charging infrastructure slowdown
Earlier this year, when it was first reported that Labour was considering watering down its EV targets, the electric vehicle charging sector warned that weakening the Government's framework could slow investment, EV adoption, and charger deployment.
In July, Guy Bartlett, chief executive of charging network Believ, said: 'We have committed over £300 million of private investment to build EV charging infrastructure ahead of demand, supporting the 35 to 40 per cent of UK households without access to a driveway.
'That investment was made on the strength of the ZEV mandate.
'Any softening of the framework risks slowing EV uptake, creating greater uncertainty for infrastructure investment and making it harder to justify rollout in lower-utilisation areas.
'That would directly disadvantage drivers and communities relying on public charging.'
Plug-in hybrid sales are soaring thanks to Chinese carmakers offering a variety of long-range, affordable PHEVs
In March, carmakers issued an urgent plea to the Government to relax electric vehicle sales targets.
Through industry lobby group the Society of Motor Manufacturers and Traders (SMMT), carmakers have been pushing for reform because the recent growth in EV sales has come at an unsustainable cost: manufacturers are spending billions of pounds on discounts and incentives to meet increasingly demanding sales quotas.
The result is that the trade body says that level of financial support cannot continue indefinitely.
As such, the expectation that the Government will relax its targets and allow more profitable combustion-engined vehicles to remain on sale beyond 2030 will be welcomed by lobbying automotive companies.
Should the Government reduce the pure-EV requirement to 55 per cent, then hybrids could account for just under half of all new-car registrations.
In particular, the Department for Transport has proposed reconsidering the role of plug-in hybrid electric vehicles (PHEVs) within the legislation and examining how motorists can be encouraged to use them in electric mode more frequently.

articles.title_orig: FDA orders new warning labels on Ozempic, Wegovy over rare risk of permanent vision loss
articles.title_zh: FDA orders new warning labels on Ozempic, Wegovy over rare risk of permanent vision loss
articles.content_orig:
The U.S. Food and Drug Administration is requiring new safety warnings on all GLP-1 drugs after finding evidence of a potential increased risk of a rare eye condition, the agency said on Monday.
The condition, which can cause sudden vision loss, known as nonarteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy (NAION), is rare, and a causal relationship has not been established.
The FDA is requiring the makers of all GLP-1 medications to add a warning about the potential increased risk of NAION associated with use of these medications, it said.
NAION is a condition that can result in sudden decreased vision, including permanent vision loss. It is caused by decreased blood flow to the front part of the ​optic nerve — the underlying cause is not completely understood, however.
NAION cases have been reported for all currently marketed GLP-1 products, the FDA said.
Ozempic and Wegovy maker Novo Nordisk said it "continues to believe the data do not establish a cause-and-effect relationship, and we remain confident in the benefit-risk profile of our GLP-1 medicines."
CNBC has reached out to Eli Lilly, the company behind Mounjaro, Zepbound and Foundayo, for comment.
The FDA decision follows a review of clinical trials, real-world patient data, and published studies.
An analysis of 126 trials involving more than 134,000 patients found 6.4 cases of NAION per 100,000 patient-years among GLP-1 users, compared with 3.8 among patients receiving other treatments or placebos.
Several observational studies also identified an increased risk, supporting the FDA's concerns.
The FDA's class-wide labeling action is "likely to attract attention but should have limited impact on GLP-1 uptake," according to Citi analysts.
It may temporarily increase patient and investor concern, but the rarity of NAION and substantial weight, glycemic, cardiovascular, renal, and sleep apnea benefits should preserve a favorable benefit-risk profile and limit changes to prescribing the medicines, they added.
While GLP-1 drugs have been shown to lead to benefits beyond weight loss and controlling blood sugar levels, many also carry the FDA's strongest safety warning, known as a boxed warning, over a potential risk of thyroid tumors.
Studies have shown that semaglutide, the active ingredient in Wegovy and Ozempic, and tirzepatide, the active ingredient in Mounjaro, cause thyroid C-cell tumors in rodents. It remains unknown whether the drugs cause these tumors, including a rare form of thyroid cancer, in humans.

articles.title_orig: U.S., Russia and Ukraine begin talks in Abu Dhabi aimed at ending war in Ukraine
articles.title_zh: U.S., Russia and Ukraine begin talks in Abu Dhabi aimed at ending war in Ukraine
articles.content_orig:
The United States, Ukraine and Russia have started talks in Abu Dhabi on Tuesday aimed at ending the war in Ukraine that began in 2022 when Russian President Vladimir Putin launched a full-scale invasion of his country's neighbor .
The two-day session is the first such meeting since February and will focus on security guarantees, a long-running demand from Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelenskyy.
President Trump's son-in-law Jared Kushner said in a post on X that he and Special Envoy Steve Witkoff were "working hard to find a negotiated solution that can deliver lasting peace and create the conditions for a sovereign, secure, and prosperous Ukraine within a more stable European security environment."
Kushner indicated these talks are just an initial step but could "build momentum" toward future negotiations. He also suggested a future agreement would involve a security arrangement involving European countries and Russia.
But on Tuesday both Russia and Ukraine seemed to pour cold water on the initiative.
Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov said Russia rejects European demands for a ceasefire in Ukraine, asserting that Brussels was just trying to "buy time" for Kyiv.
"We will not agree to this," he said.
He added that Moscow did not want to prevent the U.S. from engaging with Europe on the Ukraine war, but it does not consider that to be the best approach.
Ukraine argues that an immediate ceasefire is the necessary first step toward negotiating a wider settlement and says a direct meeting between Putin and Zelenskyy is the only way territorial issues can be settled.
Zelenskyy posted on Telegram , meanwhile, that the U.S. had asked if Kyiv would "'trade the Donbas for security," but that the U.S. said that did not mean Ukraine joining NATO, "'but something similar.'"
"No one believes that Putin will stop if we give up the Donbas," he added. "He might pause — but then he will return in a year, two years, or five years. And who will be to blame then?"
Putin has previously said he wanted Ukraine to pull its troops back from Donetsk, Luhansk, Zaporizhzhia and Kherson, the four regions Moscow illegally annexed in September 2022 but never fully captured. He also demanded that Ukraine abandon its bid to join NATO, accept strict limits on its military and drop restrictions on the Russian language and the Moscow-affiliated Orthodox Church in Ukraine.
Zelenskyy rejected Putin's demands to voluntarily cede territory that Russia hasn't been able to take on the battlefield. Zelenskyy also rejected any limits on Ukraine's military or its arrangements with Western partners, which Kyiv sees as essential security guarantees to stop Moscow from invading again.
The U.S., Russia and Ukraine have held three other rounds of trilateral talks this year, in January and February, but diplomatic efforts largely stalled after Mr. Trump launched a war on Iran. Since then, Witkoff and Kushner have held various separate meetings with Putin and Zelenskyy.
In October, first lady Melania Trump's office said she had secured a temporary ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine for the Russian-occupied Ukrainian city of Oleshky for humanitarian reasons. It lasted from Oct. 28 to Nov. 1.

articles.title_orig: How GM is trying to talk used car shoppers into buying new vehicles
articles.title_zh: How GM is trying to talk used car shoppers into buying new vehicles
articles.content_orig:
Affordability challenges are pushing some buyers out of the new vehicle market. Many are choosing used cars instead.
In turn, automakers are looking for ways to compete with many of the online retailers grabbing market share in the used car market and trying to bring some of those customers back into a new vehicle.
New vehicle sales tend to be more profitable for automakers, but reselling trade-ins as used vehicles is highly profitable for dealers. Used car prices are relatively strong, but newer online retailers such as Carvana and CarMax have made the market more competitive for dealers and other incumbent used car sellers.
"The internet and technology and apps on our phone have changed every aspect of retail, and probably one of the slowest areas of retail to have adopted to online and digital shopping has been the auto industry," said Ivan Feinseth, partner, chief investment officer and director of research at Tigress Financial Partners.
General Motors is a key example of automakers' attempts to address this shifting market. The automaker has revamped its certified used vehicle program, which now operates under the CarBravo name. It's essentially an online portal through which Chevrolet, Buick and GMC dealers can list their certified used vehicles and make them available to customers all over the U.S.
About 1,615 of GM's 3,700 dealers are enrolled in the program, according to the company. The only GM brand not involved is Cadillac, which maintains its own program.
"Certified" used or "preowned" vehicles are used cars that have undergone a thorough inspection and reconditioning. They typically come with guarantees and warranties from the manufacturer.
Many automakers have certified used programs for their own cars. But GM, as part of its revamp, is using CarBravo to certify vehicles made by other automakers. A lot of those cars arrive at dealerships as trade-ins, and often dealers will sell them to wholesale auctions, said John Fitzpatrick, senior manager of the CarBravo program.
"Wholesaling doesn't bring nearly the revenue that selling it to a new customer does," he said.
GM has said it is planning to net about 250,000 sales in its CarBravo program in 2026. Fitzpatrick said he doesn't expect that even half of those will end up being new car sales.
But through CarBravo, the customer gets access to GM's dealership network for service, something Fitzpatrick says is a key differentiator between its program and growing online sellers. CarBravo vehicles come with various warranties, depending on the age and mileage on the car.
GM said the program is driving more traffic into local dealerships, where purchases are typically finalized. That creates an opportunity to convert a used car shopper into a new car buyer. So far, the automaker said about 38% of the shoppers initially looking for used cars end up buying new.
A customer who wants to buy a full-size truck can look on the website and compare used Chevrolet Silverados alongside used Ford F-150s and Ram 1500s, for example. The buyer might settle on a used truck from any of those brands, but a conversation with a dealer can push them in a different direction.
"The customer picks up the phone, but in the back of their mind, they maybe always have been a traditional, more new car customer," Fitzpatrick said.
"You've shown the customer, you're going to pay $500 [per month] for this used F-150, but you may pay $510 or $515 for this new Chevy," he said. "And now all of a sudden the customer says, yeah, maybe I can do that because I'd rather have that new vehicle than the used truck."
While the average transaction price of a new vehicle is about $50,000, the average 3-year-old used car costs about $30,000 as of September, according to Cox Automotive.
However, industry analysts say customers base their purchasing decisions on the cost of the monthly payment more than on the sticker price of the car.
New cars often come with longer-term loan options than used ones, Feinseth said, which can result in lower monthly payments.
"On a 1- or 2-year-old car, you may be only stuck with a 3- or 4-year loan," he said. "On a new car, you can get a 5-year, 6-year loan."
The share of new car loans lasting 84 months hit a new record in the third quarter, at more than 1 in 4 loans, according to Edmunds.
Meanwhile, used car prices in some affordable segments have risen, according to Cox Automotive, and about three quarters of consumers express some interest in certified cars.
But the key is building the relationship with the customer, he said. About 50% of the buyers GM has gained through the program appear to be new to the brand, meaning there is no record of them in any of the automaker's customer databases. About 70% had never visited the dealership they ended up purchasing from.
"The goal is really to get that customer engaged with the store, give them the option of building a relationship with the dealer," he said. "The dealer can really help the customer figure out what works for their budget."
It's a boon for dealers too: Customers buying warranty-backed used cars often return to the dealership for service visits — which often account for about half of a dealership's profits. GM can also sell subscriptions to connected vehicle services, such as its OnStar, which provides safety, security and navigation services.
"That is a big part of General Motors' business going forward, is to sell the software and subscription services like OnStar and eventually to the cars that are enabled with Super Cruise," GM's advanced driver-assistance system, Feinseth said.
GM isn't the only automaker trying to use its certified preowned vehicle program to lure buyers.
Detroit rival Ford Motor also certifies vehicles made by other manufacturers through its Ford Blue Advantage program. It is on track to do 450,000 total sales in 2026, more than GM's 250,000 target. It didn't specify how many of those buyers end up purchasing new vehicles.
Toyota told CNBC in an email that about 40% of its used car shoppers end up buying new instead.
Honda didn't give specifics about its program. But Lance Woelfer, American Honda's vice president of automobile sales, said conversions happen "probably every day at dealerships throughout the country."
"But it also is more about that first interaction with the consumer," Woelfer said. "And there are people in any market that prefer to buy a used vehicle, but appreciate the confidence that a [certified preowned designation] can give them."
Woelfer said those customers come back to get their vehicles serviced at a rate about 18% higher than someone who buys a non-certified used car. They also return to purchase a new car at a rate about 7% to 8% higher in the future, he said.
"It's about that first relationship that allows us to then have that customer loyalty for life," he added. "And that's where our focus is. We've been doing it a long time, and we've seen a lot of benefits from the certified business."

Israel's new parliament will be sworn in on Tuesday, as opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot seeks to oust caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.
The former army chief was tasked with forming a government by the president, after he received the backing of 67 members of the 120-seat Knesset, compared to 46 for Netanyahu.
But Eisenkot faces an uphill struggle. His bloc of four parties won 48 seats in last month's election, while Netanyahu's bloc won 53, leaving both short of a majority. He has 28 days to build a coalition, with a possible two-week extension.
Almost half of the MKs being sworn in did not serve in the previous parliament, while Arab-led parties have a record number of seats.
The outcome of the election, which was widely seen as a referendum on Netanyahu, means there is a period of uncertainty over who will form the next government. Netanyahu will remain caretaker prime minister until then - a process which could take from days to months.
One of the most dramatic results was the performance of Israel's two Arab-led alliances - the United Arab List and the Joint List - which won an unprecedented 19 seats between them following a surge in turnout among Arab voters.
The Arab parties could therefore hold the balance of power, although Netanyahu has ruled out governing with them and three of the parties in Eisenkot's bloc have opposed including them in a coalition.
On Sunday, President Isaac Herzog tasked Eisenkot with trying to form a government.
Speaking at the president's residence, the centrist Yashar party leader called for the formation of a "national emergency government" - an implicit appeal to parties to put ideological differences aside to remove Netanyahu from office.
This, he said, would "require creative and unconventional political steps".
Eisenkot said any party or MK prepared to accept four principles could join his proposed government. Those are recognition of Israel as a Jewish and democratic state; accepting the values of the Declaration of Independence; backing mandatory military, national or civilian service for all, including communities currently exempt; and recognising Hamas as a terrorist organisation and committing to dismantling its military and governing capabilities.
The four requirements, however, could present significant obstacles to Eisenkot's potential partners.
The conscription of ultra-Orthodox Jewish men, who are exempt from military service if they are in full-time religious study, was a major election issue.
The ultra-Orthodox United Torah Judaism (UTJ) and Shas parties, which won 13 seats in total, have fiercely objected to attempts to change the status quo - something that all parties in Eisenkot's bloc campaigned to do.
Eisenkot's four principles are also contentious for the Arab parties. Both emphasise equal national and civic rights for Israel's Arab citizens, who form about 20% of the population; the vast majority of Israeli Arabs are not required to serve in the military; and neither has publicly recognised Hamas as a terrorist organisation.
The Arab parties could, though, help Eisenkot form a minority government. The United Arab List, which won eight seats, has said it is willing to be part of an Eisenkot-led coalition, while the Joint List, which won 11 seats, has offered parliamentary support from the outside.
If Eisenkot accepted such an arrangement, he would still have to persuade other parties in his bloc to agree. Avigdor Lieberman, whose Yisrael Beiteinu party won seven seats, has so far refused to join a minority government dependent on Arab MKs.
In return for their support, the ultra-Orthodox parties would be likely to demand major concessions on military conscription, which might be unacceptable to most of the parties in Eisenkot's bloc.
Netanyahu - Israel's longest-serving leader - reiterated in a video on Monday his call for the formation of a government of national unity, which he said he would lead as prime minister.
He said any Zionist party - those which support Israel as a Jewish state - including opposition parties, would be eligible. He warned against a government which relied on what he called "the Islamists", an apparent reference to Arab parties.
"You cannot form a government with Hamas supporters," he said.

articles.title_orig: Rockstar Officially Confirms GTA 6 Regional Release Times - and They're Not What We Thought
articles.title_zh: Rockstar Officially Confirms GTA 6 Regional Release Times - and They're Not What We Thought
articles.content_orig:
Rockstar Games has officially confirmed the regional release times of Grand Theft Auto 6, and it largely confirms our earlier reporting - with one major caveat.
That prior reporting was based on regional PlayStation Store data unsurfaced by a GTA fan site. That site suggested we'd see a 19-hour range, with New Zealand getting the game first, while those on the other side of the international date line - eg Mexico and countries in Central and South America - getting it last.
According to the official Rockstar announcement, that information is largely accurate - but one key detail differs. In short, it looks like release times are linked to specific time zones, rather than countries. Therefore, GTA 6's release time in all regions is midnight local time.
We previously expected that once release time arrived in, for example, the Eastern United States and Canada (EST), then the game would unlock for all mainland American and Canadian players. Instead, it looks like those further west will need to wait for their own local midnight, therefore getting the game later than anticipated. Our team member Oliver, for example, is based in Vancouver on the west coast, and will therefore get the game three hours later than he would have done if it unlocked across the Canadian mainland at the same time.
As a reminder, digital pre-loads for the game have already begun - as of midnight local time on November 10th on PlayStation and midnight GMT on Xbox - so remember to start those downloads if you want to play GTA 6 as soon as it's released. I can imagine that the PlayStation and Xbox networks may bog down significantly on release day, so getting ahead of the curve makes a lot of sense. You may need to clear some space too, as the game requires up to 212GB of storage.
Once pre-loaded, the GTA 6 entry on PlayStation 5 shows a countdown to the release date, confirming the midnight timing (embedded below).
If you want to access GTA 6 early, it is possible to "move" to the New Zealand region which gets the game first. The process is easier on Xbox, requiring just a settings change and a console restart, while on PlayStation you'd need to buy the game on a new New Zealand account, with no ability to transfer the game to your main account later.
For what it's worth, I've purchased the game on my standard UK account - if I've waited this long, I can wait a few more hours.
What are your GTA 6 launch plans? Are you taking off time from work or school to play? Or are you in no hurry? Let me know in the comments below.

articles.title_orig: Rewards platform Bilt announces 'next evolution' for American consumers, small businesses
articles.title_zh: Rewards platform Bilt announces 'next evolution' for American consumers, small businesses
articles.content_orig:
Bilt unveiled its transformed Neighborhood OS on Tuesday. ( Bilt )
Bilt, best known for helping renters earn rewards on housing payments, is expanding into local commerce with a new artificial intelligence platform aimed at helping businesses attract customers while giving consumers more ways to earn rewards close to home.
The company announced Tuesday that it is launching "Bilt Neighborhood OS," which connects with existing business systems for reservations, payments, customer management and loyalty programs to help merchants reach nearby customers, personalize offers and track spending.
For consumers, the expansion could mean earning rewards and receiving personalized offers at more restaurants, retailers and other businesses they visit near home. For merchants, it could mean reaching new customers without replacing their existing technology.
Bilt describes the launch as the "next evolution" of its business, expanding the rewards network it built around housing payments into a broader platform connecting consumers, neighborhood merchants and larger organizations.
"The last tech revolution transformed how businesses sell online, but it largely left behind the businesses that make our neighborhoods special," Bilt founder and CEO Ankur Jain said in a statement.
GOOGLE EXPANDS VOLUNTARY BUYOUTS TO 5 COUNTRIES AS AI SPENDING FUELS COST CUTS
The move builds on Bilt's network of more than 8.2 million members, who generated over $12 billion in rewarded commerce at local businesses over the past 12 months, the company said.
Launched in 2021, Bilt now reaches approximately one in four U.S. apartment buildings and expects to process more than $100 billion in housing payments this year.
Bilt founder and CEO Ankur Jain gave details on Neighborhood OS to Fox News Digital. (Bilt)
The expansion includes two offerings through Bilt for Business: Neighborhood OS, which uses AI to help merchants attract customers, build loyalty and manage business activities, and Bilt Membership Platform, which allows organizations across sports , travel, hospitality, workplaces and financial services to create branded membership programs or extend existing rewards into local communities.
A neighborhood restaurant, for example, could use Neighborhood OS to identify potential customers, send targeted offers, recognize returning guests and automatically apply rewards through its existing point-of-sale system.
Bilt says its AI agents completed more than 2 million real-world actions across more than 29,000 businesses during the past 30 days, with 91% of those actions completed without human intervention.
The platform also includes Neighborhood ID, which Bilt describes as a privacy-preserving system for connecting customer experiences without exchanging raw customer data, and Neighborhood Pass, which allows eligible members to access personalized rewards and benefits at participating businesses.
To expand its reach, Bilt is partnering with payment and commerce companies including Verifone, Clover from Fiserv, Shift4, OpenTable and Grubhub. The partnerships could eventually make Neighborhood OS available to millions of merchants, with integrations and capabilities rolling out in phases beginning in 2027.
Bilt and Hyatt say they are also looking at how World of Hyatt members could be rewarded through neighborhood experiences with Bilt Neighborhood OS. Bilt added that it will partner with Meta in 2027 to provide education and business resources to small-business owners.
The platform is also giving $100,000 to the community development organization Local Initiatives Support Corporation.
"Our partnership with Bilt will test new ways to connect financial coaching and resources with people's housing goals, including pathways to homeownership, with the goal of reaching more individuals, families, and communities across the country," said Valerie White, head of National Housing Strategic Initiatives at Local Initiatives Support Corporation.
The company is targeting a sizable share of consumer spending. Bilt estimates that approximately $6.6 trillion in annual US retail and food-services spending occurs in person.
Its inaugural State of the Neighborhood study, conducted by 451 Research by S&P Global and commissioned by Bilt, surveyed 6,591 US adults. It found that two-thirds conduct at least 80% of their everyday spending within their neighborhood, while the median consumer shops within 15 miles of home.
The survey also found that 95% of respondents would try a local business at least once if they could earn points or rewards there, while 87% said rewards would make them more likely to shop at a local business more frequently.
Bilt is also expanding into professional sports, with the Phoenix Suns, Phoenix Mercury, Houston Rockets, Houston Texans, Houston Comets and Sacramento Kings planning branded fan loyalty experiences that could reward customers inside and outside stadiums, with phased launches beginning in 2027.
The effort follows Bilt's $300 million acquisition of loyalty technology company LAVA, whose technology supports programs for 56 professional sports teams, according to the company. Bilt is also working with Mastercard to extend cardholder rewards into participating neighborhood businesses.
Ankur Jain and Brian Kelly attend the Bilt Rewards Launch Party at Equinox Hotel New York at Hudson Yards on June 22, 2021, in New York City. (Sean Zanni/Patrick McMullan via Getty Images)
Jain said Bilt's focus is on helping smaller businesses compete in an increasingly technology-driven economy.
"Our number-one goal is to grow small business," Jain told Fox News Digital. He said the company wants to empower small businesses to "grow and win against large companies that have had an unfair advantage on them."
Jain also warned that efforts to restrict AI development could hurt smaller companies that stand to benefit from the technology.

"If you hamper AI, you're hurting small business across America," he said. "AI is going to be a great democratizing force in Congress."

articles.title_orig: Trump approval rating hits lowest level since September in new poll
articles.title_zh: Trump approval rating hits lowest level since September in new poll
articles.content_orig:
Westpac survey results signal growing sense of ‘helplessness’ while Jim Chalmers faces growing pressure to rein in spending
Confidence among mortgaged households has crashed to its lowest level in more than three decades amid a growing sense of “helplessness” about the economy, even as a dramatic shift in financial markets suggests there is now a strong chance of a Reserve Bank rate cut by this time next year.
The latest Westpac survey showed its consumer sentiment index sinking again in November to reach a four-year low, amid deepening pessimism about the near-term prospects for the economy .
As Labor comes under increasing pressure over persistent cost-of-living pressures , the prime minister, Anthony Albanese, played down tensions with the treasurer, Jim Chalmers.
A day after the frontbencher Murray Watt called for colleagues to stop undermining Chalmers, Albanese said: “The treasurer is doing a great job”.
The PM said he was working closely with Chalmers in the lead-up to next month’s mid-year budget update, which will include cuts to government spending as pressure mounts to contain inflation.
“This is a treasurer who’s produced a couple of budget surpluses, lower deficits, [who is] producing economic reform,” Albanese said.
Matthew Hassan, Westpac’s head of economic forecasting, said the mood among households was last this bad in 2022, when inflation was running close to 8% and after the RBA had lifted borrowing costs by 4 percentage points over the previous year.
“Prior to that, readings this weak had only ever been seen in the economy’s darkest moments: at the onset of the Covid pandemic; the height of the GFC; and during the recessions in the early 1990s and early 1980s,” Hassan said.
Hassan said while the economic backdrop was not as extreme now as it was during the pandemic and its immediate aftermath, there were “shades of Covid in the responses” from households.
Confidence in the economic outlook over the coming year reached its weakest since August 2020, the survey showed, matching a low point last recorded during the pandemic.
“The comparison with August 2020 is quite useful as that was when Melbourne went into its second lockdown and just before the government massively scaled up income support,” Hassan said.
“There was a sense of helplessness at that stage; there was nothing we could do to avoid the pandemic, and there was nothing the government could do [to avoid the pandemic]. Obviously when the jobkeeper measures were put in place that comforted a lot of people.
“There is a similar feeling of helplessness now. You can argue a substantial portion of what is happening is out of our control, such as rising fuel prices, and there’s only so much the authorities can do to cushion Australians from that impact.”
Indebted households were gloomier still, the survey showed, with pessimism among this group at its worst in records stretching back to 1994.
The latest survey comes a week after Michele Bullock, the RBA governor , warned that the year ahead would “feel like it’s a recession” thanks to persistent cost-of-living pressures alongside weak economic growth.
After five rate increases this year, nearly three in four respondents said they expected another rate hike over the coming 12 months.
Even as the mood in the community darkens, financial markets have begun factoring in the chance of lower interest rates from the middle of next year.
The implied probability of an RBA rate cut was more than 50% by August next year, according to ANZ data, and a decrease to 4.6% was fully priced in by December 2027.
Investors have been rethinking their forecasts for central bank moves alongside a rapid retreat in the global oil price.
After testing a post-Iran war high of nearly US$118 a barrel at the end of October, the global benchmark, Brent crude, has plunged by 20% to below US$94.
“Our base case is that rates do start to come down from August next year, and we don’t see any further hikes,” Hassan said.
– Additional reporting by Tom McIlroy

articles.title_orig: We’ve never seen anything like the Anthropic IPO
articles.title_zh: We’ve never seen anything like the Anthropic IPO
articles.content_orig:
Anthropic’s debut on public markets will be unlike any that’s come before it, in ways that amount to either a once-in-a-generation opportunity — or a massive financial gamble, depending on whom you ask.
The startup behind the Claude AI assistant on Tuesday set a price range for its initial public offering of $70 to $78. If it prices at the midpoint, Anthropic will raise $61 billion in its IPO. That combined with options and unvested stock would value the company at roughly $1.1 trillion. At the top of the range, Anthropic could be worth $1.4 trillion.
When Anthropic begins trading as soon as next week, there will be no analog to measure its performance against. The market has simply never seen a dedicated AI model developer go public. It is rare for a business to IPO as a public benefit corporation and, other than SpaceX , it is unheard of for any company to go public with a target valuation above $1 trillion.
Anthropic’s IPO, expected to begin marketing to investors this week, is unconventional by almost any measure. The company promised in its pre-IPO regulatory filing that its technology would “bring forth an age of miracles” while simultaneously warning it may doom humanity. Still, the promise of a once-in-a-generation technological revolution (even with 90 pages of warnings and caveats in its more-than-300-page filing) could make Anthropic the biggest IPO in history.
But there are other financial superlatives and quirks — not to mention persistent cold feet about AI on Wall Street — that will keep many investors on the sidelines.
Despite rapid revenue growth, the five-year-old company has had only one quarter of operating profit, and it is on the hook for nearly $900 billion over the next few years — money it has committed to spend on computer power and data center infrastructure.
Anthropic fans have held up its sales growth as a positive indicator of its financial health: The company brought in $17 billion in sales in the most recent quarter, up 1,127% from the same period a year earlier. And in the first nine months of this year, it recorded $33.2 billion in sales, versus just $4.6 billion in all of 2025.
But by Anthropic’s own account, that kind of growth isn’t sustainable over the long term.
“We do not expect our revenue will continue to grow at comparable rates, and we cannot assure you that it will continue to grow at all,” the company said in its pre-IPO prospectus.
At the same time, Anthropic relied on just five customers for a quarter of its sales this year. It didn’t disclose the five, but noted that some of them are also competitors.
That points to a precarious situation in which a handful of companies have outsized control over Anthropic’s future cash flow. Any one of those companies, which may be building its own AI models to compete with Claude, may decide to scale back its own spending or walk away completely at any time. Ideally, investors would want to see a more robust customer base.
Even bullish investors say that so-called concentration risk is worth keeping an eye on.
Paul Marino, chief revenue officer at Themes ETFs, told CNN the relatively small number of major customers “gives me a little bit of concern” because their needs could change on a dime. “It’s something to monitor, but I’m not overly concerned with it because I’m one of those people that believes that AI is the future.”
Normally, when a company goes public, insiders can’t simply dump their shares on Day One and cash out — they have to hold on to them, usually for at least three to six months, to prevent the stock price from tanking.
Anthropic’s lock-up schedule may be the most convoluted of any IPO in recent memory. The company opted for a complex, staggered schedule that permits some “non-founder” insiders to sell 10% of their holdings on Day One. The prospectus then lists some 23 dates over the first year when non-founder employees can dump more shares.
Critics see that unorthodox schedule as another red flag, given the roughly $130 billion Wall Street insiders and venture capitalists have already poured into the company.
“It has maxed out private investors, who now need the company to tap public markets to get them their payday,” financial research firm New Constructs wrote in a blog post .
David Trainer, New Constructs’ founder and CEO, added in a call with CNN that he sees the payout to insiders as “a horrific misallocation of capital.”
“We’re going to make a lot of people rich… that’s value that is taken away from public investors who are effectively giving them that from their own pockets, from their retirement accounts.”
The concentration risk isn’t limited to Anthropic’s business customers. Critics also point to the concentration of power in the company’s special ownership structure, which gives its seven founders a majority of shareholder voting power. That novel approach has become more common in tech companies in recent years, but nonetheless raises concerns from some government officials.
“We’re seeing a very worrisome trend of disempowerment to shareholders and all the balance of power tipping towards management,” New York City comptroller Mark Levine told Bloomberg News.
Anthropic’s investor roadshow this week could hardly come at a worse moment for AI sentiment on Wall Street and beyond. Last week, AI-linked stocks tumbled on investors’ concerns that Democratic wins in Congress and state governments would slow the data center buildout. Americans’ sentiment about AI safety is in the gutter . And on Monday, Nvidia shares fell 5% after CEO Jensen Huang admitted to having an affair as his company announced it would be investigating him over foreign intelligence concerns.
Anthropic, which declined to comment to CNN on its IPO plans, appears to be pressing ahead despite the turmoil. The Wall Street Journal reported Monday that the company had meetings lined up with key investors this week and plans to list its shares Thursday or Friday next week, citing people familiar with the matter.

articles.content_orig:
SOFIA — The 6th China-Central and Eastern Europe High-Level Think Tank Scholars Forum, themed "China-Europe Dialogue: Expanding Synergies and Embracing a Win-Win Future," was held on Monday, bringing together more than 100 experts and scholars from Bulgaria, Croatia, Romania, Serbia and other countries.
Wang Junwei, director of the Academic and Editorial Committee of the Institute of Party History and Literature of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee, said in his keynote speech that seeking common ground while preserving differences and pursuing cooperation for mutual benefit are important principles guiding China's approach to international relations and valuable experience in ensuring the steady development of China-Europe relations. These principles will continue to play a guiding role in cooperation between China and Central and Eastern European countries (CEEC) in the future, he said.
In her welcome remarks, Chinese Ambassador to Bulgaria Dai Qingli said that as long as China and Europe uphold mutual respect and engage in equal-footed consultations, both sides will be able to find solutions to problems and continuously expand the scope for mutually beneficial cooperation.
Nataliya Kiselova, former president of the National Assembly of Bulgaria, said in her remarks that the fifth plenary session of the 20th Central Committee of the CPC demonstrated the CPC leadership's courage to uphold the truth and curb abuses of power, and its determination to continue consolidating its position as the core of leadership in Chinese society.

Wu Haitao, vice president of the China Public Diplomacy Association, said that think-tank exchanges serve as an important channel for continuously strengthening the public-opinion foundation of China-Europe friendship.
Participants held in-depth discussions on China's 15th Five-Year Plan, the four major global initiatives, global governance, and the prospects and vision for China-EU relations.
The inaugural forum was held in 2016. Since then, it has played an active role in facilitating exchanges of ideas and building consensus among think-tank scholars from China and CEEC.

articles.title_orig: U.S. moves military aircraft from British base amid Iran threats
articles.title_zh: U.S. moves military aircraft from British base amid Iran threats
articles.content_orig:
BREAKING: Inflation posts slowest rise in three months as gas prices drop
LONDON — The United States has moved military aircraft from an airbase in the United Kingdom amid threats from Iran.
A U.S. official confirmed to NBC News that several military aircraft had left RAF Mildenhall as the security posture there had increased.
They were operating under “enhanced force protection measures,” the official said. They would not speculate on the exact nature of the threat that appears to have led to ramped up security.
At least eight air refueling tankers and three Ospreys left the base in Suffolk, eastern England, on Monday, flight tracking data showed.
Some of the tankers, Boeing KC-135 Stratotankers, were relocated to airbases in Germany and Spain, with one moved to the area of Glasgow Prestwick Airport in Scotland. The Ospreys were moved to nearby RAF Lakenheath in Suffolk.
It comes weeks after the U.S. withdrew bombers from another base in Britain , RAF Fairford, after police foiled a suspected terror plot linked to Iran. The U.S. has used bases in the U.K. to strike the Islamic Republic.
The Wall Street Journal was first to report on this week’s movements and said the evacuation came following a threat from Iran, citing people familiar with the matter. It said the exact nature of the threat was not yet known and remained under discussion by U.S. officials.
“We take proactive measures to ensure our aircraft, our people, and our installations remain safe and secure,” a U.S. official told NBC News.
“U.S. Air Force aircraft rotate between installations and operating locations for a variety of reasons including training and real world requirement,” a U.S. European Command official said. “U.S. military aircraft are hosted in accordance with access, basing, and overflight agreements with our Allies and partners. Due to operations security, we will not provide further information on movement of assets,” the European Command official added.
A spokesperson for the U.K.’s Ministry of Defense said it does “not routinely comment on the activity of other nations.”
“Aircraft and other assets move regularly according to operational requirements,” the spokesperson said.
It comes weeks after the U.S. pulled aircraft from RAF Fairford following reports of a possible Iranian drone attack, two U.S. officials previously told NBC News. That move came in the wake of an investigation into a possible planned terrorist attack at that base, located in Gloucestershire.
Five men were detained on Sept. 27 after three suspicious vans were spotted traveling toward RAF Fairford. Other arrests followed and two men were charged under the National Security Act.
The incident, which attracted huge international attention, remains largely unexplained although British Prime Minister Andy Burnham said the activity was likely to have been coordinated in Iran.
Though Tehran has denied involvement in any plot against RAF Fairford, its powerful Revolutionary Guard warned in July that any base used to launch attacks against Iranian territory was a legitimate target.
Iran has vowed retaliation for any renewal of the American-Israeli war against it and has threatened to expand its response beyond the Middle East.
Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Monday that Washington had addressed concerns around reported threats from Tehran against American diplomats overseas by “moving people away from the threat.”
“Obviously, we’re always worried about the safety and security of our personnel and their families overseas,” Rubio said. “And so, when we see anything that could pose a potential threat beyond a certain threshold, we’re going to address it.”
Citing new “momentum” in negotiations to end the war, President Donald Trump on Monday downplayed the prospect of new U.S. attacks.
“Iran militarily is effectively over,” Trump said following a meeting with Qatar’s Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al-Thani.
Further U.S. attacks “won’t be necessary” at this point, but Washington remains “locked and loaded” should circumstances change, Trump told reporters at the White House.

articles.source: Breaking News, Latest News and Videos
articles.content_orig:
Discontent over prices helped fuel a Democratic landslide in the midterms.
Inflation slowed in October from September, according to a government report released on Tuesday, offering a positive sign for consumers in the first snapshot of prices nationwide since the midterm elections.
Prices rose 0.4% in October, after having climbed 0.6% in September. The monthly increase in October matched the rise in August.
The report, however, is missing a key data point: the change in prices compared to a year ago. That figure, which usually draws close scrutiny, cannot be calculated because the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) did not publish an inflation report last October amid the government shutdown.
The Iran war drove up gasoline prices and catapulted annual inflation to a three-year high in the spring. Inflation eased over the summer, but continued unrest has kept price increases well above pre-war levels.
Prices increased 3.7% over the year ending in September, the most recent month for which annual inflation data is available. In August, annual inflation was 3.4%. The annual inflation rate currently stands more than a percentage point above the Federal Reserve's target rate of 2%.
Fuel prices have accounted for a sizable share of overall inflation in recent months. Gas prices jumped more than 9% in September from August, accounting for more than half of the overall price increase last month, the most recent month on record, the BLS said.
A cooldown in oil prices since the midterm elections has put downward pressure on gasoline prices, leaving the national average price of a gallon of gas below $4 as of Monday, GasBuddy data showed. The relief at the pump in recent days did not appear in the report on Tuesday, however, since it details prices in October.
The fresh data arrived at a delicate moment for the central bank, where policymakers are weighing a rate increase that could help tackle inflation but risks a slowdown in hiring.
A stronger-than-expected jobs report last week may ease possible concern among central bankers about a cooldown for the labor market.
Employers added 165,000 jobs in October, well above an average of 48,000 jobs added each month over the previous year, BLS data showed.
If the Fed were to issue a rate increase at its next meeting in December, the decision would mark the central bank's second rate hike in four months, after it had gone three years without raising rates.
The combination of elevated inflation and a resilient labor market prompted the Fed to raise interest rates a quarter of a percentage point in September. That rate increase intends to help cool off inflation by slowing the economy and eating away at demand, though such a policy move typically yields results after a lag time lasting several months.
Policymakers may lose patience as they weigh whether the current level of interest rates is high enough to ease price hikes. The odds of a quarter-point rate hike at the Fed's next meeting are pegged at about 82%, according to CME Group's FedWatch Tool , a measure of market sentiment.
Days before the midterm elections, Fed policymakers opted to hold interest rates steady as they await further economic data. Still, Fed Chair Kevin Warsh vowed to cool off inflation.
"It’s our responsibility to get inflation down," Warsh said at a press conference in Washington, D.C.

articles.title_orig: Mini Review: Warhammer Survivors (PS5) - Absurdly Addictive Crossover Is a Match Made in Bullet Hell
articles.title_zh: Mini Review: Warhammer Survivors (PS5) - Absurdly Addictive Crossover Is a Match Made in Bullet Hell

Warhammer Survivors is exactly what its name suggests: a Warhammer reskin of Vampire Survivors .
Developed by licensed Warhammer studio Auroch Digital, with Vampire Survivors creator poncle partnering on the project, it's a fantastic, heartfelt adaptation right out of the gate.
Indeed, it's immediately obvious that an awful lot of care has been taken in providing poncle's world-beating gameplay formula with a fresh coat of paint. The Warhammer settings, characters, enemies, and weapons are all there — but the game also relishes in dishing out smaller references to Games Workshop's immensely popular fiction.
In particular, I was left pleasantly surprised by how often Warhammer Survivors pays tribute to the property's tabletop identity. Numerous playable characters, for example, are unlocked by finding miniature figure paints scattered across maps.
Meanwhile, power ups can include rolling damage dice — actual dice — across the battlefield, crushing your foes in the process. You can even drop giant blast radius templates on top of your enemies if you're lucky.
What I'm saying is that Auroch Digital and poncle clearly had loads of fun with this one — it's not just a simple copy and paste job that takes advantage of the Warhammer name.
Oh, and it's basically two games in one. On the main menu, you can pick between Warhammer's dark sci-fi 40,000 setting, and its high fantasy Age of Sigmar setting. Each comes with its own character roster, maps, enemy factions, objectives, upgrades, and everything else, making for a seriously robust package.
Gameplay-wise, the title offers a slight twist on the absurdly addictive Survivors structure. Stages have a 25-minute time limit instead of 30, and I'd say there's a larger emphasis on tactical thinking.
That's because specialised opponents are more prevalent, forcing you to weave your way through the hordes in a more methodical manner. At least, until you rack up so many super-powered upgrades that anything in your path just evaporates anyway.
Yep, that same progression curve that makes Vampire Survivors so insanely moreish is alive and well here, although I do think it takes a little longer to hit those truly chaotic highs because of the aforementioned tweaks.
All in all, Warhammer Survivors perfectly melds Games Workshop's property with poncle's timeless formula, resulting in another exceptional roguelike experience.

He still takes his fighting games seriously, but RPGs are his true passion. The Witcher, Persona, Dragon Quest, Mass Effect, Final Fantasy, Trails, Tales — he's played 'em all. Sitting in the park with her grandchildren one afternoon, Becky Tucker decided to overhaul her life.
As the four of them played and ran around, Becky, then 48, simply lacked the energy to join in. It was, she says now, a wake-up call.
The risk management consultant from Poole, Dorset, had been struggling with fatigue, anxiety, mood swings and hot flushes as perimenopause took hold.
And for as long as she could remember, she had experienced intense, debilitating migraines for a week every month, linked to her menstrual cycle.
She was also significantly overweight – something she had struggled with her whole life. At more than 13 stone and with a BMI of 29 – bordering on obese – Becky had spent the previous 25 years on various weight-loss plans.
They'd worked, to begin with, but then she piled on the pounds again when she returned to her usual diet of chocolate bars and what she calls 'beige stodge'.
It will be a familiar scenario to many in midlife – the pounds creep on until it no longer feels possible to shift them.
But three years on, it is no exaggeration to say that Becky is transformed. Indeed, as our photos show so clearly, she is almost unrecognisable. Fizzing with energy and an astonishing four stone lighter, she says she feels like a different woman.
Becky Tucker shed four stone by following the ZOE diet. The risk management consultant from Poole, Dorset, had  previously struggled with fatigue, anxiety, mood swings and hot flushes

And most importantly of all? She is now running around the park with her grandchildren, no longer stuck on a bench at the sidelines.
But what is extraordinary is that Becky achieved it – and she says this almost apologetically – 'without really trying'.
There was no restrictive diet, no calorie counting, and no pangs of hunger. Hi, I'm Professor Tim Spector, a medical scientist at King's College London, co-founder of ZOE and author of Good Mood Food.
I've spent decades researching how the food we eat affects our weight, mood and brain health. Now I'd like to share what I've discovered with you.
My exclusive six-week ZOE diet plan will show you how to eat your way to better health, with delicious recipes, simple changes and no calorie counting.
You could even lose up to a stone in time for the Christmas party season. And for DailyMail+ subscribers, it's completely free.

Research by Professor Spector, an honorary consulting physician and expert in epidemiology at King's College London, suggests that simple changes to our food choices can have remarkable benefits – from helping us lose weight without going hungry to improving our mood, boosting energy and potentially protecting our brains against the effects of ageing.
And now, in an exclusive new six-week newsletter series launching on Monday, October 26, the Daily Mail's readers can discover how to put his research into practice – with the chance to feel happier and healthier within days, and potentially as a bonus even lose up to a stone in time for Christmas.
Based on Professor Spector’s research at ZOE, and including recipes from his new cookbook Good Mood Food, the series will guide you, step-by-step, through a new way of eating that could transform not just your waistline, but most importantly how you feel every day.
You'll discover the surprisingly simple foods that nourish the trillions of bacteria living in your gut, why these microbes may hold the key to better mood and brain health, and how to feed them.

Halfway through, Professor Spector will make a live appearance on dailymail.com to answer readers' questions and talk about his cookbook.
And as Christmas approaches he'll reveal how to enjoy your favourite festive foods without undoing all your hard work – and, crucially, how to make these changes stick for life.
Indeed, research by Professor Spector's gut health company ZOE found that 35 per cent of around 5,000 participants lost at least 5 per cent of their body weight in just three months.
Their approach to diet has become a global phenomenon, refined through years of research involving hundreds of thousands of people.
Although more personalised recommendations are available to ZOE subscribers, anyone can follow the basic principles, for free.
Becky overhauled her diet with the help of nutrition science company ZOE, co-founded by Professor Tim Spector, the scientist at the forefront of discoveries in diet and gut health
These include eating 30 different plants a week, by making simple tweaks such as sprinkling seeds, nuts or fresh herbs over a salad or soup, or adding chopped fruit or greens to a plate.
Professor Spector encourages dieters to swap meat, particularly processed meat such as sausages, bacon and salami, for plant-based proteins including beans, lentils and chickpeas, and to aim for at least 30g of fibre a day.
However, chicken, lean meat and especially oily fish can still be enjoyed as part of his approach.
Ultra-processed foods, or UPFs – industrially-produced foods lacking in nutrients and containing cosmetic additives designed to make food irresistible to eat – are discouraged.
Instead, meals should be based on whole foods, with a rainbow of different-coloured plants to maximise nutrients.
'Studies have found that people who eat healthy diets, full of fruit, vegetables and whole grains, significantly improve their mood,' Professor Spector says.
'On the other hand, people who eat the most UPFs such as crisps, biscuits, sausages, sugary soft drinks, chicken nuggets and sugary cereal, have the biggest risk of mental health problems and dementia.

Eating more whole foods increases fibre intake – nine in ten Britons fail to get the recommended 30g a day, which can help protect against bowel cancer, cardiovascular disease and type 2 diabetes.
All ZOE studies to date have shown improvements in mood and energy within the first two weeks in the majority of people.
High-fibre foods also make you feel fuller for longer and can stimulate the release of GLP-1, the appetite-regulating hormone mimicked by weight-loss drugs.

articles.title_zh: Jensen Huang lobbied ‘very good friend’ Trump for more Nvidia sales to China while ‘caught in Beijing’s honeytrap’
articles.content_orig:
SAN FRANCISCO — Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang made himself President Trump’s “very good friend” and lobbied the administration to loosen restrictions on AI chip sales to China while he was allegedly ensnared in a Chinese honeytrap, a timeline of his reported relationship with Alice Huang shows.
The $150 billion AI boss appeared in loved-up snaps with accused communist spy Alice Huang last year — and then weeks later personally pitched Trump at the White House on relaxing export restrictions for the company’s chips.
Huang missed Trump’s second inauguration, but then more than made up for it with a $25 million donation to the president’s ballroom project.
The 63-year-old appeared at a $1 million-per-person dinner at Mar-a-Lago in April 2025, where he pushed to lift chip restrictions that had just been imposed. There were at least three documented meetings between Trump and Huang where the administration responded with policy changes that made it easier for Nvidia to sell advanced chips to China.
China hawks have long pushed to restrict the most cutting edge chips from the communist regime in an attempt to blunt its technological advances and stymie its attempts to overtake the US on AI.
Huang, for his part, had lobbied and spoken out against restrictions since the Biden administration first imposed limits in 2022. Additionally, selling more chips to the world’s second largest economy could only help Nvidia’s bottom line.
But all the while, Huang — who has been married to college sweetheart Lori for more than 40 years — was meeting with 42-year-old Alice. In May 2025, they were spotted at dinner together during Taiwan’s top tech expo, where she looked at him adoringly and affectionately touched his arm as they sat with other tech honchos.
Alice Huang — a TV host, turned banker, turned executive at the Singapore-based AI computing company Megaspeed — met Jensen Huang (no relation) in early 2024, according to reports. Megaspeed has bought billions of dollars in chips from Nvidia for data centers in Southeast Asia and the Middle East.
Separately, the firm — backed by Chinese tech giant Alibaba — is under investigation for allegedly smuggling chips to China. The US government is probing reports that 50,000 chips sold to Megaspeed were seemingly missing following an audit.
Nvidia reportedly intervened in that probe, according to Bloomberg.
The Chinese government denies allegations of a honeypot spy scheme. Megaspeed also denies allegations of wrongdoing.
Trump himself has downplayed Huang’s admission of infidelity and Nvidia’s board said the company, which has no succession plan for replacing Huang, had full confidence in him, even as it announced it was investigating the claims.
On Monday, Trump said he called to check on Huang after he admitted cheating on his wife and apologized to his family.
“I did speak to him today just to see if he’s feeling all right,” Trump said at the White House. “He said he had absolutely no idea that the person in question was a spy. I asked him that question. Did you have any idea that she was a spy? He said I had no idea that she was a spy, and I really believe him.”
The president and the Nvidia “have become good friends,” a source close to them told The Post.
Huang has made himself an integral part of the US economy. Nvidia reached a historic $5.5 trillion in valuation in May 2026, beating out Apple at the time as the most valuable public company in the entire world. It is both the world’s most important chipmaker, and the locus around which the AI boom spins. It uses the profits from its sales to help fund AI companies building out data centers, spurring further demand for its products.
By some accounts the AI boom is expected to account for up to 4% of all US economic activity this year, and Nvidia’s revenues alone up to 1%.
Trump personally hailed Nvidia’s latest quarter record sales of $96.2 billion in September, up 106% from last year.
Huang notably traveled with the president during his trip to China last May, with Trump even going as far as to personally invite the Nvidia boss to ride with him on Air Force One.
When Huang couldn’t make it to Washington DC in time for departure, he took his private plane to Alaska to join the president during his refueling stop in Anchorage.
Dressed in his signature black leather jacket and carrying only a backpack, Jensen boarded the presidential plane alone, without an entourage, pausing to speak with Trump’s son Eric, who was also on the trip, as he boarded.
Huang and his wife were seated at the head table with the president and first lady Melania Trump at the September state dinner for Chinese President Xi Jinping . Trump was personally involved in selecting the guest list for that dinner, a source familiar with the planning told The Post.
Along with the gains for his company, Huang’s relationship with Trump reportedly came with some perks of power.
Huang called the president when his invitation to the April state dinner for King Charles arrived without a plus one, according to a source. The billionaire CEO wanted to bring his wife to the dinner.
When White House staff told him there were no plus ones, he called Trump and made a personal appeal, getting Lori Huang on the list and bumping a senior administration official off of it to make room for her, multiple administration sources told The Post.
Huang has two grown children with his wife, Spencer and Madison, who both work in their father’s company.
The family has a $38 million home in San Francisco , with Nvidia spending nearly $4 million in fiscal 2026 on services for Huang that included home security, protection during personal travel, consulting and drivers, according to its May proxy filing.
Huang has remained close to Trump, literally, traveling to the Middle East for Trump’s visit to Saudi Arabia and United Arab Emirates in May 2025, then to London to join the president at Windsor Castle for a state dinner with King Charles that September.
Trump, at a meeting with then-British Prime Minister Keir Starmer during that visit, saw the CEO in the audience and teasingly told him: “You’re taking over the world Jensen. I don’t know what you’re doing here. I hope you’re right.”
He also had a prime seat at Trump’s side at the September 29th meeting on AI policy , alongside other technology executives. And the president awarded him the National Medal of Science last month.
Huang and Trump remained close friends despite the warning signs about the Nvidia boss’ relationship with Alice, which one tech company flagged to the Commerce Department last summer.
“The White House has known how suspicious Ms. Huang, and her corporate network, is since last summer,” a source familiar with the case told The Post. “And Jensen has repeatedly lied about his relationship with Ms. Huang.”
Culper Research also published a report titled “NVIDIA (NVDA): The China Problem” in May 2026, which specifically warned about the concerning rumors about Nvidia’s chief executive and Alice.
Alice had been under investigation since the Biden administration and believed to have been recruited as an asset for China’s feared Ministry of State Security.
The Commerce Department first flagged Alice following her sudden rise to the top of Megaspeed in 2023.
The concerns were troubling enough that Secretary of State Marco Rubio pushed back on letting Huang attend the China state dinner with Trump, the source added.
